label: Dimensions
what: The size of what you selected, plus flip and rotate.
when: When a shape is too big or small for the hoop, or sits the wrong way round.
typical: A suit-lining logo is often 40 to 80 mm wide.

label: Width
what: How wide the selection is, in millimetres or inches.
when: When the design needs to fit a hoop or a garment spot.
typical: 40 to 80 mm for a lining logo.
effects: With the padlock on, height follows.

label: Height
what: How tall the selection is.
when: When a design must fit a tall, narrow spot like a cuff.
typical: Matches the width when the padlock is on.

label: Lock aspect ratio
what: Keeps width and height in proportion when you resize.
when: Leave it on to avoid squashing a logo. Turn it off to stretch on purpose.

label: Keep aspect ratio
what: When on, changing width also changes height.
when: Leave it on for logos and letters. Turn it off to stretch a shape.
typical: On. Hold Ctrl while dragging a handle to flip it for one drag.

label: Units
what: Shows sizes in millimetres or inches.
when: When your garment spec or hoop is listed in inches.

label: Flip left-right
what: Mirrors the selection from left to right.
when: When a design faces the wrong way, like a crest that must mirror a pair.
typical: Use once, then check the result.

label: Flip top-bottom
what: Mirrors the selection upside down.
when: When you need a reflection, or a design was drawn upside down.

label: Rotate 90 degrees
what: Turns the selection a quarter turn clockwise.
when: When a design is sideways, or to fit a tall hoop.
typical: Press again for a half turn.

label: Colour
what: The thread this shape is sewn in.
when: When the digitizer picked a nearby thread you want to change.
typical: A real thread from your brand or My Threads.

label: Region colour
what: Override the thread used for every region you click.
when: When you want one colour for several regions, like a gold crest.
typical: Leave on automatic to keep the matched colours.

label: Style
what: Filled sews the whole area. Outlined sews only the edge.
when: When a shape should be a solid patch or only a border.
typical: Filled for big areas, outlined for borders.

label: Outlined or filled
what: Switch a closed shape between a solid fill and an edge line.
when: When you want a hat patch border or a solid badge face.

label: Region style
what: Sew each clicked region as a fill or as an outline.
when: Outline thin regions. Fill big ones.

label: Run type
what: How a line is sewn: single, triple, satin, E-stitch, rope or manual.
when: When a line should be bolder, wider or decorative.
typical: Single for fine lines, satin for borders.

label: Stitch length
what: The distance between needle drops along a line.
when: Lengthen for a loose line, shorten for tight curves.
effects: Shorter means more stitches and a heavier line.

label: Tolerance
what: How far a stitch may stray from the curve you drew.
when: Lower it when curves look faceted. Raise it for fewer stitches.

label: Width
what: How far E-stitch teeth reach, or how wide a rope twist is.
when: Widen E-stitch for appliqué edges. Keep rope thin.

label: Flipped
what: Puts the E-stitch teeth on the other side of the line.
when: When the teeth point into the shape instead of away.

label: Single run
what: One line of stitches. The everyday running stitch.
when: For fine outlines, stems and details.

label: Triple run
what: Each stitch goes forward, back and forward again for a bold line.
when: For outlines that must stand out or thin details.
typical: Use in place of a satin under 1.5 mm.

label: Satin run
what: A column of fixed width with thread across it.
when: For borders and letter strokes from 2 to 6 mm.

label: E-stitch
what: Comb-shaped stitches reaching out from the line.
when: For appliqué edges and decorative borders.

label: Double rope
what: A thin twisted cord sewn in two passes.
when: For a braid border, like piping round a patch.

label: Triple rope
what: A thicker twisted cord sewn in three passes.
when: For a bolder braid.

label: Manual run
what: Sews exactly the stitch points you placed, in order.
when: For touch-ups and converted files.
typical: Made with the Manual stitch tool.

label: Satin
what: Settings for satin columns: spacing, edge compensation and underlay.
when: When satin looks gappy, bumpy or puckers the cloth.
typical: Start with the defaults and test sew.

label: Satin width
what: The width of the satin column.
when: Widen for a bolder border. Under 1.5 mm use a triple run.

label: Density (spacing)
what: The gap between needle drops on one side. Smaller is denser.
when: Tighten if cloth shows through. Loosen if thread breaks or cloth puckers.

label: Pull compensation
what: Widens each side because thread pulls the cloth in.
when: Raise it if sewn columns come out narrower than drawn.

label: Split above
what: Splits columns wider than this into stitched halves.
when: For wide columns, so long stitches do not snag.

label: Stagger cycles
what: How many stitches before the split line pattern repeats.
when: When the join of a split column shows as a visible seam.

label: Stagger amount
what: How far the split line moves sideways between stitches.
when: Use with stagger cycles to hide the seam.

label: Short stitches on curves
what: Shortens stitches on the inside of tight curves.
when: For round letters and curved borders where stitches bunch up.

label: Satin underlay
what: Light stitches sewn under the column to lift it and hold the cloth.
when: Always use some under columns wider than 1.5 mm.
typical: Centre run under 2.5 mm. Wider, add edge and zig-zag.

label: Fill pattern
what: The texture of the fill. Each preview shows a 40 by 30 mm shape.
when: When a plain fill looks flat, or you want a brick, wave or ring effect.

label: Pattern setting
what: A setting specific to the pattern you picked.
when: When the pattern's shapes or lines are too big, small or tight.
typical: The default shown when you pick the pattern.

label: Draw guide curve
what: Draw a curve the pattern's lines should follow.
when: For flow-line patterns that need to follow a petal or wave.

label: Stitching
what: Settings every fill shares: angle, spacing, length and edge.
when: When a fill looks too dense, too sparse or runs the wrong way.

label: Angle
what: The direction of the stitch rows, clockwise from the right.
when: When rows should follow the shape, or catch the light differently.

label: Angle dial
what: Turn the stitch angle with a dial on the canvas.
when: When you want to set the angle by eye.

label: Row spacing
what: The distance between rows of stitches. Smaller is denser.
when: Raise it if the fill puckers or breaks thread. Lower it if cloth shows.
effects: Smaller means more stitches and a stiffer fill.

label: Stitch length
what: The longest stitch along a row.
when: Shorten for tight curves, lengthen for a smoother sheen.
typical: 3 to 4 mm. Machines snag above 12 mm.

label: Pull compensation
what: Grows the fill so it matches your drawing after the cloth pulls in.
when: When a sewn fill is smaller than drawn or leaves a gap at its outline.
typical: 0.2 mm, up to 0.4 mm on knits.

label: Hand stitch
what: Adds a small random wobble so the fill looks hand-sewn.
when: For a craft look, not for logos.

label: Underpath
what: Travels through the fill, hidden, instead of jumping between rows.
when: When a fill has many jumps or trims.

label: Edge outline
what: Sews a thin running line round the edge after the fill.
when: For a clean border on fills that look ragged at the edge.

label: Gradient
what: Makes the rows thin out across the shape, like a fade.
when: For a soft shading effect on a big fill.

label: Gradient type
what: None, ramp (fades one way) or plateau (dense in the middle).
when: Pick ramp for sunsets, plateau for a glowing centre.

label: Start spacing
what: Row spacing at the start, as a multiple of normal spacing.
when: To control how dense the fade begins.

label: End spacing
what: Row spacing at the far end, as a multiple. Bigger is sparser.
when: To control how sparse the fade ends.

label: Middle spacing
what: Row spacing in the middle of a plateau. Bigger is sparser.
when: For plateau fades that thin toward both ends.

label: Reverse gradient
what: Flips the gradient so it fades the other way.
when: When the fade runs toward the wrong side.

label: Underlay
what: Light stitches sewn first, under the fill, to hold the cloth flat.
when: Add passes for heavy fills on soft cloth.

label: Fill underlay
what: Adds one light pass at right angles to the fill.
when: For any fill larger than a few millimetres.

label: Underlay angle
what: The direction of an underlay pass.
when: Cross passes at different angles for heavy fills.

label: Underlay spacing
what: The gap between rows of an underlay pass.
when: Tighter for heavy fills, wider for light cloth.

label: Underlay stitch length
what: The stitch length of an underlay pass.
when: Rarely. Shorter for tight curves.

label: Underlay inset
what: How far inside the edge the underlay stops, so it stays hidden.
when: Raise it if underlay shows at the edge.

label: Map to path
what: These shapes are copies placed along a path.
when: To change how many copies there are, or turn them into plain shapes.

label: Placement
what: Spread copies by count or by spacing along the path.
when: By count for an exact number of stars. By spacing for an even rhythm.

label: Copies
what: How many copies sit along the path.
when: When you need an exact number, like seven stars.

label: Map spacing
what: The distance along the path from one copy to the next.
when: When copies crowd each other or leave gaps.

label: Rotate to follow the path
what: Turns each copy as the path turns.
when: For leaves along a vine. Leave off for upright stars.

label: Reverse direction
what: Starts the copies from the other end of the path.
when: When the first copy lands at the wrong end.

label: Open image
what: Choose a PNG, JPG, WEBP or SVG to turn into stitches.
when: To start a design from a logo or drawing.

label: Colours
what: How many thread colours the picture is reduced to.
when: Lower it to cut thread changes. Raise it for more detail.
effects: Each colour is one thread swap.

label: Size
what: The width and height of the finished design in millimetres.
when: Set it before you digitize, so detail is sized right.
typical: 80 to 100 mm for fine serif logos.

label: Lock aspect ratio
what: Keeps the picture's proportions when you set the size.
when: Leave on so the logo does not squash.

label: Smallest region
what: Drops specks smaller than this many square millimetres.
when: Raise it if you see dust-like dots in the result.

label: Background
what: Remove treats the picture's background as bare cloth. Keep stitches it.
when: Keep only if the background is part of the design.

label: Thread brand
what: The thread range colours are matched to.
when: Choose the brand you own or plan to buy.

label: Quality
what: Standard is quick and predictable. Premium follows each column's width.
when: Pick Premium for fine logos and small letters.
typical: Standard for tests, Premium for the real run.
effects: Premium makes about 1.3 times the stitches.

label: Thread weight
what: 40 wt is standard thread. 60 wt is finer, for small detail.
when: Use 60 wt for letters under 6 mm.

label: Fabric
what: What you are sewing on. It tunes spacing, underlay and compensation.
when: Set it to match your garment before you digitize.
typical: Suiting for jackets, shirting for lining.

label: Use my threads
what: Match colours to the spools on your My Threads shelf first.
when: When you want a design you can sew from your own drawer.
typical: On once your shelf is filled in.

label: Digitize
what: Runs the auto digitizer with the current settings.
when: After changing size, colours, quality or fabric.
typical: Press it again after each change.

label: Click to stitch
what: Choose which traced regions to stitch, one click at a time.
when: When you want control over which parts get stitched.

label: Threads used
what: The real threads the design uses.
when: To check the shopping list before you sew.

label: Hoop
what: The embroidery area of your machine. Shapes outside it cannot be sewn.
when: At the start of a design, and when you change machine.
typical: The hoop you will sew in.

label: Hoop chip
what: Shows the current hoop. Click to open the hoop list.
when: To change hoop or search by brand and machine.

label: Smallest hoop that fits
what: Picks the smallest hoop that holds the whole design.
when: After you resize, to see which hoop to put on.

label: Swap width and height
what: Turns the hoop between landscape and portrait.
when: When a tall design nearly fits a wide hoop.
typical: Try it before a bigger hoop.

label: Add my own hoop
what: Save a custom hoop with your own width and height.
when: When your hoop is not in the list.
typical: Measure the sewing area, not the frame.

label: Show hoop frame
what: Draws the frame and its clamp around the sewing area.
when: When you want the canvas to look like the real hoop.

label: Show safe margin
what: A dashed line 5 mm inside the sewing area.
when: To keep stitches clear of the frame and presser foot.

label: Show rulers
what: Rulers along the top and left. Drag from one to pull out a guide.
when: To line shapes up exactly.

label: Placement guide
what: A guide showing where a design usually sits, like a cuff or pocket.
when: When placing a monogram or crest on a garment.

label: Actual size
what: Shows the design at its true size on your screen.
when: To judge size against a real garment.

label: Calibrate screen
what: Teaches Lilo how big a millimetre is on your display.
when: Once, before you rely on Actual size.
typical: Hold a ruler to the screen.

label: Drawing colour
what: New shapes are drawn in this thread.
when: Before you draw, to avoid recolouring later.
typical: The thread you plan to use first.

label: Sewing setup
what: Shows your fabric, thread weight and quality. Click to change.
when: When you change fabric, thread or machine.

label: Fabric
what: What you are sewing on. Lilo adjusts spacing, underlay and edge compensation.
when: Whenever the cloth changes.
typical: Suiting, shirting, twill, knit, denim, towel or leather.

label: Thread weight
what: 40 wt is standard. 60 wt is finer and allows smaller detail.
when: Use 60 wt for small letters.

label: Quality
what: Standard is quick. Premium takes more care over each column.
when: Premium for fine logos, Standard for tests.

label: Before you sew
what: Needle, stabiliser, topping and hooping tips for your setup.
when: Read it before every real sew-out.
typical: Follow it, then sew a test.

label: File format
what: The file type your machine reads.
when: Match it to your machine. Brother and Baby Lock use PES.
typical: PES for Brother, DST for commercial machines.

label: Export stats
what: Stitches, colour changes, size and time for this file.
when: Check them before you save.
typical: Look for surprises, like a huge stitch count.

label: File name
what: The name of the saved file. Lilo adds the right ending.
when: Use plain letters and numbers for USB sticks.

label: Origin point
what: Which point of the design sits at the hoop's zero.
when: Change it only if your machine starts from a corner.

label: Save
what: Writes the file where you choose.
when: When the stats and warnings look right.
typical: The root of a USB stick.

label: Machine
what: Which saved machine receives the file.
when: When you have more than one machine.
typical: The machine on your own Wi-Fi.

label: Search network
what: Looks for machines on your Wi-Fi.
when: When your machine is missing from the list.
typical: The machine must be on and on 2.4 GHz.

label: Send
what: Sends the design to the chosen machine over Wi-Fi.
when: After checking Before you sew.

label: Play
what: Plays the design stitch by stitch.
when: To check the order and the thread changes.

label: Scrub stitches
what: Drag to jump to any point in the sew.
when: To inspect one part, or go back to the start.

label: Speed
what: How fast playback runs, from 1 times to 50 times.
when: Slow to inspect, fast to skip ahead.

label: Auto-continue
what: Carries on after each colour change instead of waiting.
when: Turn it off to practise your thread swaps.

label: Design totals
what: Stitch count, colour changes, size and estimated sewing time.
when: To plan your day or spot a heavy design.

label: Sequencer views
what: Switch between objects, colours, images and My Threads.
when: To change order, merge colours or add a reference picture.

label: Move up or down
what: Changes the order a shape is sewn in.
when: When a fill covers an outline, or you want fewer jumps.

label: Hide or show
what: Takes a shape off the canvas and out of the file.
when: To check one layer at a time.
typical: Show it again before you export.

label: Rename
what: Double-click a name to rename a shape.
when: To keep a big design easy to read.
typical: Short names like Border or Leaf.

label: Details
what: Shows the stitch and point counts for a shape.
when: To find the shape that makes the file heavy.

label: Group by colour
what: Reorders shapes so each colour is sewn in one block.
when: When a thread is used in several places and you want fewer swaps.
typical: Use it, then play the design to check.

label: Merge into
what: Folds one colour into another.
when: When two colours are close and one swap is enough.

label: Swap thread
what: Replaces a thread with another everywhere it is used.
when: When you do not have that spool.

label: Select objects
what: Selects every shape in this colour.
when: To resize or edit one colour together.

label: Add image
what: Puts a reference picture behind the design. It is not stitched.
when: To trace over a sketch or compare to the original.

label: Image opacity
what: How see-through the reference picture is.
when: Lower it so stitches stay easy to see.

label: Image width
what: The reference picture's width in millimetres.
when: To match the picture to your design.
typical: The same as the design width.

label: Select tool
what: Click to select, drag to move, drag empty space to box-select.
when: For most editing. Shift adds to the selection.

label: Pan tool
what: Drag to move the view.
when: When zoomed in. Hold Space to pan with any tool.

label: Measure tool
what: Drag between two points to read the distance.
when: To check a crest against a hoop or a garment spot.

label: Open shape tool
what: Click to add points. Enter finishes. Double-click makes a curve point.
when: For stems, borders and lines.

label: Closed shape tool
what: Like Open shape, but the outline closes into a fill.
when: For leaves, badge outlines and solid areas.

label: Circle tool
what: Drag a box for an ellipse. Hold Ctrl for a perfect circle.
when: For round hat patches and dots.

label: Rectangle tool
what: Drag a box. Hold Ctrl for a square.
when: For labels, bars and frames.

label: Pen tool
what: Draw freehand. Lilo smooths the line when you let go.
when: For signatures and loose sketches.

label: Satin blocks tool
what: Click the left edge, then the right edge, and repeat along a column.
when: For curved borders where you control each stitch angle.

label: Text tool
what: Click where text goes, then type in the panel.
when: For names, initials and monograms.

label: Click to stitch tool
what: Click regions of a traced picture to stitch them.
when: When you want to choose which parts get stitched.
typical: Key K. Open an image first.

label: Manual stitch tool
what: Click to place each needle drop exactly.
when: For small touch-ups.

label: Undo
what: Steps back one edit.
when: After any change you do not like.
typical: Command Z. Sliders undo as one step.

label: Redo
what: Brings back an edit you undid.
when: When you undid too far.

label: Drawing colour
what: The thread your next shape will use.
when: Before you draw a new shape.

label: Toolbar help
what: Lists every tool with what it does and when to use it.
when: When you do not know which tool to pick.

label: Reshape
what: Move, add and delete a shape's points.
when: To fix an outline. Double-click a point to switch corner and curve.

label: Cut hole
what: Draw a closed shape inside a fill to cut it out.
when: For the middle of an O, or a ring.
typical: One closed shape inside the fill.

label: Knife
what: Drag a line across a shape to slice it in two.
when: To split a shape and sew the parts in different colours.

label: Start point
what: Click the canvas to choose where sewing starts.
when: To cut jumps by starting near the previous shape.

label: End point
what: Click the canvas to choose where sewing ends.
when: To finish near the next shape.

label: Angle
what: Turn the stitch direction with a dial on the canvas.
when: For fills that should follow a shape.

label: Map to path
what: Repeats the selection along an open path.
when: For stars or leaves along a line.
typical: Key P. Select the shape and a line together.

label: Outline or Fill
what: Switches a closed shape between an edge line and a solid fill.
when: When a patch needs a border instead of a solid face.

label: Redwork
what: Adds a running outline along every edge of the selection.
when: For a sketch look, or a border on many shapes.

label: Lock
what: Locks the selection so it cannot move or change.
when: When a shape is right and you do not want to nudge it.

label: Duplicate
what: Makes a copy of the selection.
when: For pairs like left and right cuffs.

label: Delete
what: Removes the selection.
when: When you no longer need a shape.

label: Shape bar help
what: Lists every shape action with what it does and when to use it.
when: When you do not know which action to pick.

label: Text to stitch
what: The words or initials to sew.
when: Type your monogram or name here.
typical: Two or three letters for a lining mark.

label: Letter height
what: How tall a capital letter is, in millimetres.
when: Set it before choosing a font. Small letters need care.
typical: 6 mm minimum with 40 wt thread, 4 mm with 60 wt.

label: Height presets
what: Quick heights: 6, 10, 15 and 25 mm.
when: For a fast start.

label: Letter spacing
what: The gap between letters.
when: Open it up for elegant caps. Tighten if letters look loose.

label: Line spacing
what: The gap between lines of text.
when: For text with more than one line.

label: Alignment
what: Left, centre or right for text with more than one line.
when: Centre for crests, left for labels.

label: Curve
what: Bend the text round the top or bottom of a circle.
when: For the edge of a round hat patch or a crest. Straight suits everything else.
typical: Arc up on top, arc down along the bottom.
effects: A curve centres the text, so Alignment is ignored.

label: Curve radius
what: The size of the circle the letters follow, in millimetres.
when: Smaller bends harder. Match it to the patch: a 50 mm patch needs about 20 mm.
effects: A radius too small for the word squashes letters together.

label: Add text
what: Adds the text to the design, or updates the selected word.
when: After you pick the text, height and font.

label: Only fonts for this height
what: Hides fonts that do not sew well at your height.
when: Leave it on while choosing.

label: Fonts
what: Built-in embroidery fonts, each drawn to be sewn.
when: When you pick a look for your letters.
typical: Choose one that suits your height.

label: Your fonts
what: Fonts you uploaded from your computer.
when: To stitch a brand's exact typeface.

label: Upload font
what: Adds a TTF, OTF or TTC font file.
when: When no built-in font matches your brand.

label: Realistic
what: Draws stitches as shaded thread, thicker for satin and rope.
when: To judge how the design will look sewn.

label: Grid
what: Shows a square grid on the canvas.
when: To line shapes up.

label: Reference
what: Shows your original picture behind the stitches.
when: To compare the stitches to the source.
typical: On while checking, off when judging.

label: Jumps
what: Shows thread that travels between shapes without sewing.
when: To spot long jumps that need trims.

label: Project name
what: The name of this project. It is also the default file name.
when: Name it after the job.

label: Search
what: Finds any tool or action by name.
when: When you do not know where a command lives.

label: Export
what: Saves the design as a machine file or a picture.
when: When you are ready for a USB stick.

label: Send
what: Sends the design to a machine over Wi-Fi.
when: When your machine is set up in Lilo Link.

label: Stitch regions
what: Stitches the regions you collected with Shift-click.
when: After picking several regions.

label: Clear selection
what: Forgets the regions waiting to be stitched.
when: If you picked the wrong ones.

label: Clear the automatic stitches
what: Removes the automatic result and keeps the bare trace.
when: To stitch only the regions you choose.

label: Back to Select
what: Leaves Click to stitch and goes back to the Select tool.
when: When you are done picking regions.

label: Add a spool by photo
what: Reads a thread label from a photo and suggests the thread.
when: To add a spool without typing its code.
typical: A sharp photo of the label.

label: Add by hand
what: Add a thread Lilo does not know by typing its brand, code and name.
when: For a spool that is not in the catalogue.

label: Search the catalogue
what: Find a thread by brand, code or name.
when: To add a spool you own.

label: Quantity
what: How many spools of this thread you own.
when: To keep track of stock.

label: Import and export
what: Saves your shelf to a file or loads one back.
when: To back up, or move to another computer.
